newsitem.title: POLAND: Foreign buying of Polish T-bills lifts zloty.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying of Polish T-bills lifts zloty.

text.p: The zloty made a late charge on Monday against the currency basket as an estimated $50 million worth of foreign investor entry and the U.S. dollar's decline on world markets lifted the Polish unit.
Dealers said foreigners rushed to buy zlotys and short-term T-bills after the morning's domestic client orders pulled the zloty down to about 1.4 percent from parity.
"The zloty slipped and speculative foreign capital quickly jumped into Polish T-bills," said one dealer in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 1.56/1.51 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Friday's close at 1.49/1.46 percent.
It closed at 3.2165/85 to the dollar, up from 3.2265/75 on Friday and at 1.8780/90 to the mark, down from 1.8640/45.

Dealers said foreigners bought nearly half of the 396 million zlotys of 13-week T-bills sold at Monday' auction with an average yield of 20.82 percent. The average yield of the 39-week T-bill was set at 21.43 percent.

The finance ministry said it would hold an additional 600 million zloty primary tender on June 11 with the value date of June 13. It has not announced the full primary auction schedule for the month of June.
